intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Paddle through a network of jungle canals in this remote Caribbean wildlife haven often called the 'Amazon of Costa Rica.' Spot caimans, river turtles, manatees, three-toed sloths, and over 300 bird species with a local naturalist guide. If visiting July–October, witness nesting sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Trek across a series of suspension bridges suspended high in the rainforest canopy surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. This self-guided eco-trail offers unparalleled views of the volcano and surrounding lake while you encounter poison dart frogs, coatis, morpho butterflies, and a dazzling variety of tropical birds in their natural habitat.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide armed with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter all four species of Costa Rican monkeys, two-toed sloths, white-nosed coatis, and rare birds along jungle trails that open onto pristine white-sand beaches with turquoise Pacific waters — a perfect blend of wildlife and beach.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek
experiences.description: Venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' This guided day hike through old-growth primary rainforest in the Osa Peninsula offers extraordinary chances to spot tapirs, scarlet macaws, harpy eagles, peccaries, and all four monkey species. A true bucket-list eco-adventure for serious wildlife enthusiasts.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Costa Rica airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, collect luggage and take a shared shuttle or public bus to Aegean Bliss Resort (budget tip: shared shuttles cost ~$15-25 vs $80+ for private taxis). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest local town on foot. Visit the central market or a local 'soda' (small Costa Rican diner) for your first authentic meal. Watch the sunset from the beach near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or after landing — grab a light snack from airport cafeteria (~$5-8)
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick bite at a roadside 'soda' near the bus stop (~$4-6 for a casado plate)
meals.dinner: Dine at a local 'soda' near the resort — try Casado (rice, beans, plantains, protein) for ~$5-8

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones at the airport for better rates. Buy a local SIM card (~$10-15) for data. Confirm resort check-in time in advance. February is dry season — expect sunny, warm weather.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a self-guided beachfront nature walk along the coast. Look for coastal wildlife including pelicans, frigate birds, and hermit crabs. Bring water and sunscreen. This activity is completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife reserve (many have entry fees of $5-18 for budget travelers). Explore walking trails, spot howler monkeys, iguanas, and tropical birds. Ask resort staff for the closest budget-friendly reserve.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and relax on the beach. Head to a local 'soda' or beachside kiosk for dinner. Chat with other budget travelers to share tips and potential activity partners.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit from a local market or roadside vendor (~$2-3). Cook instant oats if resort has a kitchen, or find a soda offering a $3-5 gallo pinto breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich or buy from a local bakery (panadería) near the park entrance (~$3-5)
meals.dinner: Local soda near the beach — try Arroz con Pollo or fresh fish plate (~$6-9)

day_by_day.notes: Carry insect repellent and wear light, breathable clothing. Download the iNaturalist app to identify wildlife you spot. Mornings are best for wildlife activity before the heat peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group zip-lining tour. Look for local operators offering group rates (~$35-55 per person vs $80+ for tourist packages). Many zip-line parks open at 8am — book the earliest slot for cooler temperatures and better wildlife sightings in the forest canopy.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, explore the surrounding cloud or rainforest on a self-guided trail near the zip-line park. Look for toucans, sloths, and colorful tree frogs. Many parks include basic trail access with the zip-line ticket.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit a local farmers' market if one is running nearby. Relax with a locally brewed Imperial beer (~$1.50) or fresh coconut water from a street vendor (~$1-2).

meals.breakfast: Gallo Pinto (rice and beans with egg) at a local soda before the tour (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Many zip-line parks have an on-site cafeteria — budget $6-10 or pack your own lunch
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the resort if kitchen is available, or visit a local soda (~$5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining tours through local operators or hostel boards rather than hotel concierge to save 20-40%. Wear closed-toe shoes and secure any loose items. Check if the tour includes transport — group shuttles are often included.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public bus or shared ride to a nearby wildlife sanctuary or rescue center (entry ~$10-20). These centers rescue and rehabilitate sloths, monkeys, toucans, and other Costa Rican wildlife. Far more ethical and affordable than private wildlife tours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the sanctuary, explore a nearby waterfall on foot. Many waterfalls near coastal areas have free or low-cost ($2-5) access via marked trails. Bring a swimsuit for a refreshing dip in the natural pool.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the resort area. Stroll the local town and browse artisan markets for budget souvenirs (handmade crafts, coffee, chocolate). Enjoy street food for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit plate from a roadside vendor (~$2-4) plus local coffee (~$1)
meals.lunch: Picnic near the waterfall — buy supplies from a local mini-super (small grocery store) (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Street food: empanadas, patacones, or chifrijo from a local food stand (~$3-6)

day_by_day.notes: Research wildlife sanctuaries carefully — choose accredited centers that prioritize animal welfare over tourist interaction. Avoid any place that allows selfies with wild animals. Waterfall trails can be slippery — wear water shoes or sturdy sandals.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for a guided bird-watching walk. Costa Rica has over 900 bird species. Join a small group tour (~$20-30) or hire a local birding guide for a 2-hour walk. Look for scarlet macaws, toucans, motmots, and tanagers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local cacao or coffee plantation for a budget tour (~$15-25). Learn how Costa Rica's famous coffee and chocolate are produced. Many tours include tastings. This is a great way to support local farmers directly.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event in the nearest town — check for community festivals, live music at local bars, or free beach bonfires. February can feature local celebrations.

meals.breakfast: Early morning before birding: grab a coffee and pan dulce (sweet bread) from a local bakery (~$2-3)
meals.lunch: On-site lunch at the plantation or nearby soda (~$5-8)
meals.dinner: Try a local comedor (family-run restaurant) for a traditional Costa Rican dinner (~$6-10)

day_by_day.notes: Birding is best at dawn (5:30-8:00am) when birds are most active. Bring binoculars if possible — some tour operators lend them. February's dry season means clear skies and excellent visibility for bird-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public bus to a nearby national park known for wildlife (Carara, Manuel Antonio, or Tortuguero depending on your resort location). Arrive early to maximize wildlife spotting. National park entry ~$18 for foreigners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon hiking park trails. Look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, coatis, Jesus Christ lizards (basilisks), and sea turtles on nearby beaches. Stick to marked trails to minimize environmental impact.
day_by_day.evening: Return via public bus to the resort. Enjoy a relaxing evening on the beach. Watch for bioluminescence in the ocean if conditions are right — a magical free natural phenomenon.

meals.breakfast: Gallo Pinto at a soda near the bus stop (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch from a mini-super to save money inside the park (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood at a local beachside restaurant — ceviche or grilled fish (~$8-12)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase national park tickets online in advance if possible — some parks (like Manuel Antonio) have daily visitor caps and sell out during peak season. February is peak dry season so book ahead. Bring at least 2 liters of water per person.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning. Sleep in, enjoy the resort's beachfront, and do laundry (hand wash or find a local laundromat ~$3-5). This is a good mid-trip recovery day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle from a local shop (~$8-15/day) and explore the surrounding coastal roads and villages. Stop at viewpoints, small beaches, and local shops along the route.
day_by_day.evening: Join other travelers for a budget cooking class or attend a free salsa dancing lesson if available locally. Alternatively, cook a simple meal using fresh market ingredients if the resort has kitchen access.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer breakfast at a local café — smoothie bowl or pancakes with tropical fruit (~$5-8)
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh coconut and snacks from a beach vendor (~$3-5)
meals.dinner: Cook at the resort using fresh local ingredients from the market (~$5-8 for groceries) or visit a local soda

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest days are important on eco-adventure trips to prevent fatigue. Use this time to review remaining activities, confirm any bookings, and reorganize your gear. Check weather forecasts for the coming days.

day_by_day.morning: Book a white-water rafting or kayaking excursion on a nearby river. Look for budget group tours (~$35-65 per person). Class II-III rapids are suitable for beginners and offer excellent wildlife viewing along riverbanks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After rafting, visit a nearby hot spring (many are free or low-cost natural springs, not commercial resorts). Soak tired muscles in natural thermal waters. Ask locals for directions to the best free springs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Visit a local bar for a cold Imperial beer and watch a Costa Rican football (soccer) match on TV — a great way to connect with locals.

meals.breakfast: Energy-packed breakfast before rafting: eggs, rice, beans, and fruit at a local soda (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: Most rafting tours include a riverside lunch — confirm when booking. Budget $0 (included) or $6-8 if separate.
meals.dinner: Local soda or comedor near the resort (~$6-9)

day_by_day.notes: Rafting operators provide all safety equipment. Wear quick-dry clothing and secure all valuables in waterproof bags provided. River wildlife includes kingfishers, herons, crocodiles (on some rivers), and river otters.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided mangrove kayaking or boat tour through coastal mangroves (~$20-40 for group tours). Mangroves are incredible ecosystems hosting crocodiles, herons, egrets, and juvenile fish. Early morning is best for wildlife activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach that's off the main tourist trail — ask resort staff or locals for their favorite hidden beaches. Snorkel if equipment is available for rent (~$5-10) and explore coral formations and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach walk collecting shells. Have dinner at a beachside 'chiringuito' (beach bar/restaurant). Try a fresh ceviche appetizer with a tropical juice.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before kayaking: banana and peanut butter sandwich (~$2-3)
meals.lunch: Fresh fish tacos from a beachside stand (~$5-8)
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant — grilled whole fish with rice, beans, and salad (~$9-14)

day_by_day.notes: Mangrove ecosystems are fragile — follow guide instructions and avoid touching roots or wildlife. Snorkeling is best in calm, clear conditions. February's dry season typically provides excellent visibility. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby volcano or volcanic landscape. Many volcanoes in Costa Rica have budget access via public buses (~$2-5 each way) and national park entry fees (~$15-18). Hike crater rim trails with panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the volcanic surroundings — look for unique flora adapted to volcanic soils, sulfur vents, and volcanic lakes. Many volcanic parks have multiple trails of varying difficulty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by public bus. Visit a local farmacia (pharmacy) or mini-super to restock supplies. Enjoy a quiet dinner and early bedtime to recover from the day's hiking.

meals.breakfast: Pack a hearty breakfast from the resort or soda before the early bus departure (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch for the volcano hike — sandwiches, fruit, and trail mix (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Simple meal at a local soda or cook at the resort (~$5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Volcanic areas can be cool and misty even in dry season — bring a light rain jacket and an extra layer. Altitude can be significant at some volcanoes (Arenal: 1,670m, Poás: 2,700m). Stay on marked trails near active volcanic areas for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a nearby cloud forest or nature reserve on a self-guided hike. Cloud forests are dramatically different from lowland rainforests — cooler, misty, and home to resplendent quetzals, glass frogs, and orchids. Entry fees typically $5-15.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a community-based tourism experience — look for local cooperatives offering chocolate-making workshops, traditional cooking classes, or craft demonstrations (~$10-25). Money goes directly to local communities.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free ranger talk or conservation presentation at a local national park visitor center. Many parks offer these free educational programs in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Gallo Pinto and local coffee at a soda near the forest entrance (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Community lunch as part of the tourism experience, or local soda (~$5-8)
meals.dinner: Try a local vegetarian restaurant or comedor for a budget-friendly plant-based Costa Rican meal (~$5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Cloud forests are typically cooler than coastal areas — pack a light jacket. Rubber boots are sometimes available for rent at cloud forest reserves ($2-3) which are very useful on muddy trails. Quetzal sightings are more common during February nesting season.

day_by_day.morning: Final full adventure day: book a canopy tour or hanging bridges walk through the rainforest (~$25-45 for budget operators). Hanging bridges offer a different perspective from zip-lining — slower, quieter, and excellent for wildlife photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach for a final swim and relaxation session. Rent a surfboard for a beginner lesson if interested (~$20-30 including instruction). Costa Rica's Pacific coast has gentle waves perfect for beginners.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with fellow travelers. Splurge slightly on a nicer local restaurant for a special final dinner — fresh seafood platter or traditional Costa Rican feast. Budget $12-20 for a memorable meal.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit smoothie and toast at a local café (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: Beach snacks and fresh coconut water from vendors (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered — treat yourself! (~$12-20)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to purchase final souvenirs — locally produced coffee ($5-10/bag), dark chocolate ($3-5/bar), and handmade crafts are the best value. Pack items carefully to avoid damage. Confirm your departure logistics for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort. Wake up for one last sunrise beach walk and wildlife spotting. Take photos of the beachfront and write down your favorite memories. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort — confirm checkout time the night before.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: travel to the airport via shared shuttle or public bus. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5-3 hours before your international flight. Browse duty-free for any last-minute gifts (coffee and rum are great budget options).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica. Reflect on 13 incredible days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, and budget-savvy exploration. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda — savor it! (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Airport food or a final soda meal before heading to the airport (~$5-10)
meals.dinner: Airplane meal or airport restaurant depending on flight time

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: A well-planned 13-day Costa Rica budget trip can be done for $60-90 USD per day including accommodation, food, activities, and transport. Keep receipts for any travel insurance claims. Leave no trace — Costa Rica's natural beauty depends on responsible tourism. Consider donating to a local conservation organization before you leave.

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Trek across a series of suspension bridges suspended high in the rainforest canopy surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. This self-guided eco-trail offers unparalleled views of the volcano and surrounding lake while you encounter poison dart frogs, coatis, morpho butterflies, and a dazzling variety of tropical birds in their natural habitat.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort on the beachfront (approximately 2–3 hours depending on location). Enjoy the scenic coastal drive and check in. Freshen up and take a relaxed stroll along the beach to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the beachfront near the resort. Explore the immediate surroundings, pick up any essentials from a local tienda, and enjoy a quiet first night settling in.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport – Café Britt or a local soda (Costa Rican casual diner) inside the terminal
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's on-site restaurant – try a classic Casado (rice, beans, plantains, salad, and protein) to kick off the trip with authentic Costa Rican flavors. Budget ~$15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm all upcoming tour bookings upon check-in. Exchange currency or withdraw colones from an ATM at the airport. Stay hydrated – Costa Rica's humidity can be intense for new arrivals.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided beachfront wildlife walk along the coastline near the resort. Look for scarlet macaws, howler monkeys, and coastal bird species common to Costa Rica's Pacific or Caribbean shore. A local naturalist guide can be arranged through the resort (approx. $30–40 per person for 2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife refuge accessible from the resort area. Explore mangrove trails or a local nature reserve. Rent a kayak or paddleboard from the resort to explore calm coastal waters and spot marine wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a cocktail at the beach bar while watching the sunset. Explore a local open-air restaurant in the nearest town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or order Gallo Pinto (rice and beans with eggs) – a quintessential Costa Rican morning staple. Budget ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch packed by the resort or stop at a local soda near the nature reserve – try Arroz con Pollo or fresh ceviche. Budget ~$8–15.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local beachfront seafood restaurant – fresh grilled fish, patacones (fried plantains), and a cold Imperial beer. Budget ~$18–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Apply sunscreen and insect repellent before all outdoor activities. Wear light, moisture-wicking clothing. This day is designed to ease into the eco-adventure pace before more intense excursions begin.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by shuttle or rental car toward Arenal Volcano National Park (travel time varies by resort location – typically 3–5 hours from Pacific coast). Enjoy the scenic highland drive through rolling hills and farmland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a mid-range lodge near Arenal (e.g., Arenal Backpackers Resort or Hotel La Fortuna). After settling in, embark on the featured experience: **Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Walk** – trek across a series of suspension bridges high in the rainforest canopy surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. Spot toucans, sloths, poison dart frogs, and coatis. Approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Soak tired muscles in the famous natural hot springs near Arenal (Tabacón, Baldi, or the free public hot springs at La Fortuna Waterfall area). Enjoy a relaxed dinner in La Fortuna town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – Gallo Pinto with fresh tropical fruit and coffee. Budget ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside soda en route to Arenal – try a hearty Casado or Olla de Carne (beef and vegetable stew). Budget ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local La Fortuna restaurant such as Soda Viquez or Rancho La Cascada – traditional Costa Rican cuisine with volcano views. Budget ~$15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Hanging Bridges tour in advance. Wear sturdy closed-toe hiking shoes. The hanging bridges walk is moderate difficulty and suitable for most fitness levels. Bring a rain jacket – the Arenal rainforest receives frequent afternoon showers in any season.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to **La Fortuna Waterfall** – a spectacular 70-meter cascade set deep in the rainforest. Hike down 500+ steps to the base and swim in the natural pool. Arrive before 8:00 AM to beat crowds. Entry ~$18 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: White-water rafting on the Balsa or Toro River near Arenal (Class II–III, suitable for beginners to intermediate). A guided half-day rafting experience typically costs $50–75 per person and includes equipment and a snack.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna lodge. Enjoy a leisurely evening stroll around La Fortuna town. Browse local artisan shops for souvenirs and handcrafted goods.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before the waterfall hike – eggs, toast, tropical fruit, and Costa Rican coffee. Budget ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Post-rafting lunch at a riverside open-air restaurant – grilled tilapia with rice, beans, and salad. Budget ~$12–18.
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Jardín restaurant in La Fortuna – wood-fired pizza or pasta with local ingredients in a garden setting. Budget ~$15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The waterfall hike is steep – trekking poles are helpful. Water shoes are recommended for the swimming pool at the base. Book rafting in advance through the lodge or a local operator. Stay hydrated throughout both activities.

day_by_day.morning: Guided wildlife and birdwatching tour around Lake Arenal – spot kingfishers, herons, ospreys, and potentially a Jesus Christ lizard (basilisk) walking on water. A 2-hour boat tour on the lake offers excellent wildlife viewing. Cost ~$35–50 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel by jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal toward Monteverde (approximately 3 hours total, a classic and scenic Costa Rican journey). Check in to a mid-range Monteverde lodge (e.g., Hotel Belmar or Monteverde Lodge).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Monteverde town center. Explore the Cheese Factory (Productores de Monteverde) – a local institution producing artisan cheeses since the 1950s. Enjoy a quiet evening walk through the misty village.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure. Budget ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the lodge or stop at a soda en route during the jeep-boat-jeep transfer. Budget ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Morpho's in Monteverde – a beloved local spot serving hearty Costa Rican meals with excellent vegetarian options. Budget ~$15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer is a highlight of the trip and far more scenic than driving around the lake. Book tickets in advance through your lodge ($25–35 per person). Roads into Monteverde are unpaved and bumpy – prepare for a rugged final stretch.

day_by_day.morning: The headline experience of the trip: **Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour** – soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Multiple platforms, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges included. Operators such as Selvatura Park or Original Canopy Tour offer 2–3 hour experiences. Cost ~$45–65 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the **Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve** – one of the most biodiverse ecosystems on Earth. Walk guided trails through the mystical cloud forest, searching for resplendent quetzals (February is prime nesting season!), glass frogs, and orchids. Guided tour ~$20–30 plus entry fee of ~$25.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a **Night Walk** in the cloud forest – a guided after-dark excursion revealing nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, sleeping birds, tree frogs, and insects. Cost ~$25–35 per person.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before the zip-line tour. Budget ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Colibri near the reserve – sandwiches, soups, and fresh juices in a hummingbird garden setting. Budget ~$10–16.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tree House Restaurant in Santa Elena – dine inside a 100-year-old fig tree in a multi-level restaurant with creative Costa Rican-fusion cuisine. Budget ~$18–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal in Monteverde – this is a bucket-list sighting. Wear layers – the cloud forest sits at 1,500m elevation and can be cool and misty. Waterproof jacket essential. Book all three activities in advance as they fill quickly on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Visit **Selvatura Park's Hummingbird Garden and Butterfly Garden** – observe 30+ hummingbird species feeding at close range and explore one of the largest butterfly exhibits in Central America. A peaceful and photographic morning. Entry ~$15–20 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recharge day. Optional: visit the **Monteverde Orchid Garden** (home to 425+ orchid species) or browse local artisan markets in Santa Elena for handcrafted jewelry, paintings, and coffee. Alternatively, book a coffee or chocolate farm tour (~$25–35 per person) to learn about Costa Rica's agricultural heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewpoint visit – hike or drive to a local mirador (lookout) for panoramic views over the Gulf of Nicoya and the Pacific coast. On clear evenings, you may see Arenal Volcano in the distance.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the lodge – fresh fruit, yogurt, and granola with local coffee. Budget ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Soda La Esperanza in Santa Elena – a no-frills local soda with enormous portions of traditional food at great value. Budget ~$7–11.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Monteverde at Restaurante El Sapo Dorado – upscale-casual dining with international and Costa Rican cuisine, mountain views, and live music on weekends. Budget ~$22–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is a lighter recovery day before travel resumes. Use the afternoon to do laundry if needed, charge devices, and reorganize luggage. Consider purchasing locally grown Monteverde coffee as a gift or souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided birdwatching walk in the cloud forest reserve or surrounding private reserves (Children's Eternal Rainforest). February is peak nesting season – an expert guide maximizes wildlife sightings. Cost ~$30–45 per person for 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Monteverde by shuttle toward the Pacific Coast (Manuel Antonio area or Quepos – approximately 4–5 hours). Check in to a mid-range coastal lodge or boutique hotel. Spend the late afternoon relaxing on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Quepos town – a lively fishing village with excellent waterfront restaurants, local bars, and a vibrant atmosphere. Enjoy a sunset from the malecón (boardwalk).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before departure. Budget ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside soda en route – try Sopa Negra (black bean soup) or a fresh empanada. Budget ~$7–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Quepos waterfront restaurant – fresh catch of the day (pargo, mahi-mahi, or dorado) with patacones and a tropical fruit juice. Budget ~$18–26 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The road from Monteverde to the Pacific coast is partially unpaved – if renting a car, a 4x4 is strongly recommended. Alternatively, shared shuttles are comfortable and cost-effective (~$35–50 per person). Confirm accommodation before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day visit to **Manuel Antonio National Park** – one of Costa Rica's most celebrated parks. Enter early (gates open at 7:00 AM) to maximize wildlife sightings. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, squirrel monkeys (endangered), raccoons, and hundreds of bird species along jungle trails leading to pristine beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the park's beaches – Playa Manuel Antonio and Playa Biesanz offer crystal-clear waters for swimming and snorkeling. Bring snorkel gear to explore the coral reef near the rocky point. The park closes at 4:00 PM – exit and relax at your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking the Pacific (Barba Roja or La Luna are popular). Enjoy the famous Manuel Antonio golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before entering the park – fruit, eggs, and coffee at the hotel. Budget ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch inside the park (pack food from town as park vendors are limited) – sandwiches, fruit, and plenty of water. Budget ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Agua Azul restaurant in Manuel Antonio – creative seafood and Costa Rican dishes with ocean views. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Manuel Antonio National Park entry in advance online – the park limits daily visitors and sells out during peak season. February is high season, so early booking is essential. Hire a certified naturalist guide at the park entrance (~$25–35) to dramatically improve wildlife spotting. Keep all food securely stored – capuchin monkeys are bold thieves!

day_by_day.morning: Guided sea kayaking and snorkeling tour along the Manuel Antonio coastline – paddle through calm Pacific waters, explore sea caves, and snorkel around rocky outcrops teeming with marine life including parrotfish, sea turtles, and rays. Half-day tour ~$55–75 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife rescue center near Manuel Antonio (e.g., Kids Saving the Rainforest or Titi Conservation Alliance) – learn about Costa Rica's wildlife rehabilitation efforts and see recovering animals up close. Entry ~$15–20 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class experience in Quepos or Manuel Antonio – learn to prepare traditional Costa Rican dishes such as Gallo Pinto, Olla de Carne, and Tres Leches cake with a local chef. Cost ~$55–75 per person including dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before the kayaking tour. Budget ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Post-kayaking lunch at a beachside soda – ceviche, rice, and fresh coconut water. Budget ~$10–16.
meals.dinner: Dinner IS the cooking class – enjoy the meal you prepare with your group. A truly memorable and delicious experience.

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen only – regular sunscreen is harmful to coral reefs and is prohibited in many protected areas. The cooking class should be booked at least 2 days in advance. This is a great evening for solo travelers and couples alike.

day_by_day.morning: Guided horseback riding tour through the rainforest and along the beach near Manuel Antonio or Dominical (approximately 2 hours). A unique way to experience the landscape and spot wildlife from a different vantage point. Cost ~$45–65 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel back toward the resort area (Aegean Bliss Resort, beachfront) – arrange shuttle or drive (timing depends on resort location). Check back in and decompress. Spend the late afternoon at the resort pool or beach.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome-back dinner at the resort. Enjoy a leisurely evening on the beachfront – stargazing, beach walk, or a bonfire if the resort offers one.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Manuel Antonio hotel before horseback riding. Budget ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Lunch en route – stop at a local soda or roadside restaurant. Try Sopa de Mariscos (seafood soup) if available. Budget ~$10–16.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant – splurge slightly on a nice seafood platter to celebrate the final stretch of the trip. Budget ~$22–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm shuttle bookings from Manuel Antonio back to the resort area the day before. If driving a rental car, check return policies and fuel requirements. This travel day should be kept relatively light on activities.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day at the resort – morning yoga session on the beach (many resorts offer complimentary or low-cost classes) followed by a relaxing swim in the ocean. Enjoy the beachfront at its finest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional half-day tour: guided mangrove kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding excursion near the resort. Alternatively, book a local boat tour to spot dolphins, sea turtles, or whale sharks if in season. Cost ~$35–55 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner – celebrate the final evening in Costa Rica with a special meal. Dress up slightly and choose a nicer local restaurant near the resort or a beachfront dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast – full spread with tropical fruits, eggs, and the best Costa Rican coffee you've had all trip. Budget ~$12–18.
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at the resort bar – ceviche, fresh coconut, and a tropical smoothie. Budget ~$12–18.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the finest local restaurant near the resort – splurge on a multi-course meal with fresh seafood, local ingredients, and a bottle of Chilean or Argentine wine. Budget ~$35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to purchase any remaining souvenirs and gifts – locally produced coffee, chocolate, hot sauce, and artisan crafts make excellent take-homes. Pack bags tonight to avoid morning rush. Confirm airport transfer for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the beachfront – a peaceful goodbye to the Pacific. Enjoy a last Gallo Pinto breakfast at the resort. Complete packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Juan Santamaría International Airport via pre-arranged private shuttle or shared transfer. Arrive at the airport with at least 3 hours before your international flight. Browse the duty-free shops for last-minute souvenirs – Café Britt coffee, Amor chocolate, and local rum are popular choices.
day_by_day.evening: Board your return flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of cloud forests, volcanoes, wildlife, zip-lines, and Pacific sunsets in one of the world's most biodiverse countries.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – savor every bite of that Gallo Pinto! Budget ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the airport – Café Britt restaurant or a local soda inside the terminal. Budget ~$12–18.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for airport check-in during Costa Rica's high season (February) – lines can be long. Keep your passport, boarding pass, and any receipts for customs declarations easily accessible. Costa Rica charges a departure tax that is typically included in international airfare but confirm this in advance. ¡Pura Vida!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Paddle through a network of jungle canals in this remote Caribbean wildlife haven often called the 'Amazon of Costa Rica.' Spot caimans, river turtles, manatees, three-toed sloths, and over 300 bird species with a local naturalist guide. If visiting July–October, witness nesting sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Trek across a series of suspension bridges suspended high in the rainforest canopy surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. This self-guided eco-trail offers unparalleled views of the volcano and surrounding lake while you encounter poison dart frogs, coatis, morpho butterflies, and a dazzling variety of tropical birds in their natural habitat.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide armed with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter all four species of Costa Rican monkeys, two-toed sloths, white-nosed coatis, and rare birds along jungle trails that open onto pristine white-sand beaches with turquoise Pacific waters — a perfect blend of wildlife and beach.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek
experiences.description: Venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' This guided day hike through old-growth primary rainforest in the Osa Peninsula offers extraordinary chances to spot tapirs, scarlet macaws, harpy eagles, peccaries, and all four monkey species. A true bucket-list eco-adventure for serious wildlife enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Private luxury transfer from Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) to Aegean Bliss Resort arranged with a personal concierge greeting at arrivals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private welcome orientation with resort concierge. Settle into your beachfront suite, enjoy a complimentary welcome cocktail and fruit platter on your private terrace. Light exploration of the resort grounds and beachfront at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the private beach. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport lounge prior to arrival
meals.lunch: Welcome amenities and light bites provided upon check-in at the resort
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant — fresh ceviche, grilled pargo (red snapper), and tropical desserts paired with a curated Costa Rican craft cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all luggage is handled by resort porters. Confirm next-day activity bookings with concierge. Rest and hydrate well after the long-haul flight. Dress code at the restaurant is smart-casual.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided sunrise kayaking tour along the coastline near the resort. Explore sea caves, spot marine iguanas, and enjoy the golden morning light on the Pacific with a certified naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour — explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide armed with a high-powered spotting scope. Spot sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs along pristine jungle trails that open onto white-sand beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a private outdoor jungle shower experience and sunset cocktails on the terrace. Dinner at a renowned farm-to-table restaurant in the Manuel Antonio area.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast buffet at the resort featuring tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, freshly baked pastries, and Costa Rican gallo pinto
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed inside Manuel Antonio National Park overlooking the beach
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Luna Restaurant (Manuel Antonio area) — known for Mediterranean-Costa Rican fusion, fresh seafood, and panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Wear light breathable clothing and sturdy walking shoes for the park. Apply reef-safe sunscreen and bring insect repellent. Manuel Antonio is approximately 10–15 minutes from the resort. Book park entry in advance as daily visitor numbers are capped.

day_by_day.morning: Private sport fishing charter departing from Quepos Marina. Target world-class offshore species including sailfish, mahi-mahi, and yellowfin tuna aboard a fully equipped luxury fishing vessel with an experienced captain and first mate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to marina by early afternoon. Afternoon at leisure — relax at the resort's infinity pool with personalized cocktail service, or enjoy a rejuvenating 90-minute couples' massage at the resort spa featuring volcanic stone therapy.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfront bonfire dinner experience arranged by the resort — a personal chef prepares a multi-course tasting menu under the stars with the sound of the Pacific waves.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departing for the marina — fresh fruit, granola, yogurt parfait, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard lunch catered on the fishing charter — fresh ceviche, tropical salads, cold cuts, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Private beachfront chef's table dinner — courses include lobster bisque, grilled catch of the day (potentially your own morning catch), passion fruit sorbet, and a premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Confirm fishing charter reservation at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Bring motion sickness medication if needed. The private bonfire dinner must be pre-arranged with the resort's culinary team — request at check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter transfer from the Manuel Antonio area to the Osa Peninsula — a breathtaking 30-minute scenic flight over the Pacific coastline, rainforest, and the Gulf of Dulce offering unparalleled aerial wildlife spotting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Corcovado National Park Day Trek — venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' A guided trek through primary rainforest reveals tapirs, giant anteaters, jaguars (elusive but present), scarlet macaws, and an extraordinary density of wildlife found nowhere else on the planet.
day_by_day.evening: Private boat transfer back across the Gulf of Dulce. Helicopter return to the resort or overnight stay at a luxury eco-lodge near the Osa Peninsula (optional upgrade).

meals.breakfast: Pre-departure gourmet breakfast at the resort — eggs your way, smoked salmon, avocado toast, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch provided by the trekking operator, enjoyed at a scenic jungle clearing inside Corcovado — sandwiches, tropical fruit, energy bars, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Martina (Drake Bay area) or return to the resort for a late à la carte dinner at the resort restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires a licensed guide by law — all guides are pre-certified naturalists. Wear waterproof hiking boots, long pants, and long sleeves. Bring a dry bag for electronics. The helicopter transfer is weather-dependent — have a ground transport backup plan. This is a full and physically demanding day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast followed by a private yoga session on the beachfront deck with a certified instructor as the sun rises over the Pacific. Optional: guided meditation session in the resort's jungle garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling and catamaran sailing excursion along the Manuel Antonio coastline. Snorkel vibrant coral reefs, spot sea turtles, tropical fish, and rays. Swim in secluded coves accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail cruise aboard the catamaran returning to port. Dinner at a top-rated restaurant in Quepos.

meals.breakfast: Healthy wellness breakfast at the resort — acai bowls, fresh-pressed green juice, chia pudding, tropical fruit platters, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard catering during the catamaran excursion — fresh sushi rolls, shrimp cocktail, ceviche, tropical fruit, and premium open bar
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Patio de Café Milagro (Quepos) — celebrated local institution known for creative Costa Rican cuisine, fresh seafood, and an award-winning rum cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Bring biodegradable reef-safe sunscreen for the snorkeling excursion — standard sunscreen is banned near marine protected areas in Costa Rica. The catamaran excursion typically runs 4–6 hours. Book through the resort concierge for a private charter.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury ground transfer from Manuel Antonio to Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 4–5 hours with scenic stops). Stop at a premium artisanal coffee estate en route for a private estate tour and cupping session featuring single-origin Costa Rican beans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde. Check into a luxury cloud forest lodge (pre-arranged by concierge). Afternoon at leisure — explore the resort grounds, visit the Orchid Garden, or enjoy a private guided birdwatching walk to spot resplendent quetzals, toucans, and hummingbirds.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the Monteverde continental divide viewpoint, then dinner at the lodge's acclaimed restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — full gourmet spread
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the coffee estate or a curated roadside stop at a premium local restaurant in the Central Valley featuring traditional Costa Rican casado
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Monteverde lodge restaurant — cloud forest-inspired cuisine featuring heart of palm salad, beef tenderloin with chimichurri, and warm chocolate lava cake with local honey ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The road to Monteverde includes some unpaved sections — a 4x4 luxury SUV transfer is recommended. Temperatures in Monteverde are significantly cooler (15–22°C / 60–72°F) — pack a light jacket and layers. Monteverde is approximately 1,440 meters above sea level.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience multiple cables, Tarzan swings, rappels, and sky bridges suspended above the emerald treetops with panoramic cloud forest views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walk through the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve with a senior naturalist guide. Explore primary and secondary cloud forest ecosystems, spot howler monkeys, coatis, and extraordinary epiphytic plants. Optional: night walk to spot nocturnal species including kinkajous, glass frogs, and sleeping birds.
day_by_day.evening: Artisanal cheese and wine tasting at a local Monteverde dairy farm (the region is famous for its Swiss-influenced cheese-making tradition). Return to lodge for a nightcap by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Hearty lodge breakfast — scrambled eggs with local cheese, gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruit, and Costa Rican drip coffee
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at Taco Taco or Sofia Restaurant in Santa Elena — creative Latin fusion cuisine in a relaxed premium setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tree House Restaurant (Santa Elena) — a remarkable dining experience built around a 700-year-old strangler fig tree, serving elevated Costa Rican cuisine

day_by_day.notes: The zip-line tour typically has a weight limit of 113 kg (250 lbs) per participant — confirm in advance. Closed-toe shoes are mandatory. The cloud forest can be misty and cool — wear layers. The night walk is an additional 2–3 hour excursion beginning at dusk and requires a flashlight (provided by guide).

day_by_day.morning: Private guided birdwatching tour at dawn in the Monteverde reserve — the early morning hours offer the best chance to spot the legendary resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and emerald toucanet with an expert ornithologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Monteverde to Arenal Volcano area (approximately 2–3 hours via the Lake Arenal ferry crossing — a stunning scenic route). Check into a luxury Arenal eco-lodge with direct volcano views.
day_by_day.evening: Private soak in natural volcanic hot springs at the lodge or at a premium hot springs resort such as Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort. Enjoy the therapeutic mineral-rich waters as the jungle comes alive at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before the dawn birdwatching tour — fruit, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at a restaurant overlooking Lake Arenal en route — fresh trout, local produce, and craft beers from a regional brewery
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tabacón Grand Spa's El Tucano Restaurant — an iconic setting surrounded by thermal streams and lush tropical gardens, serving upscale Costa Rican and international cuisine

day_by_day.notes: The Lake Arenal ferry crossing takes approximately 1 hour and offers spectacular mountain and lake scenery — have cameras ready. Tabacón hot springs dinner reservations must be made in advance. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the hot springs. Arenal Volcano is occasionally cloud-covered — views vary.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Walk — trek across a series of suspension bridges suspended high in the rainforest canopy surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. A private naturalist guide identifies wildlife including poison dart frogs, sloths, toucans, and howler monkeys from the elevated vantage points.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private white-water rafting experience on the Balsa or Toro River (Class III–IV rapids) — a thrilling afternoon adventure through pristine rainforest canyons with a professional safety-certified guide team and luxury post-rafting refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset volcano viewing from the lodge terrace with a private cocktail hour. Dinner at the lodge's premier restaurant with volcano views.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the Arenal lodge — eggs Benedict with smoked local ham, fresh tropical fruit, and specialty Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Post-rafting riverside barbecue lunch prepared by the rafting operator — grilled meats, rice and beans, fresh salads, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge's signature restaurant — volcano-view dining featuring filet mignon with yuca purée, hearts of palm salad, and a premium Costa Rican craft beer or wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The hanging bridges walk is moderate difficulty — suitable for all fitness levels. The rafting excursion is more physically demanding — confirm fitness requirements with the operator. All safety equipment is provided for rafting. Volcano views are best in the early morning and evening when clouds clear.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Arenal to Tortuguero (approximately 3–4 hours via La Pavona boat dock). The journey itself is an adventure — a scenic boat ride through jungle waterways to reach this roadless Caribbean paradise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — paddle through a network of jungle canals in this remote Caribbean wildlife haven often called the 'Amazon of Costa Rica.' Spot river otters, caimans, manatees, Jesus Christ lizards, and an extraordinary array of bird species with a certified naturalist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a premium eco-lodge in Tortuguero. Sunset boat tour along the main canal for golden-hour wildlife photography. Dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure — grab-and-go option with fresh fruit, pastries, and thermos coffee for the journey
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Caribbean-style restaurant in Tortuguero village — rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, jerk chicken, and fresh patacones
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Tortuguero eco-lodge restaurant — Caribbean-influenced cuisine featuring coconut curry shrimp, plantain-crusted fish, and tropical fruit desserts

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small plane — a private charter flight is an available luxury upgrade (approximately 45 minutes from San José). Pack light for the boat journey and protect electronics from humidity and potential splashing. The Caribbean side of Costa Rica has a distinct Afro-Caribbean culture and cuisine — embrace the difference.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn sea turtle nesting/hatching observation tour (February is within the green sea turtle season). A certified guide leads a carefully managed nocturnal beach walk to witness one of nature's most extraordinary spectacles — sea turtles nesting or hatchlings making their way to the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Second Tortuguero canal wildlife boat safari focusing on deeper jungle waterways and bird-rich lagoons. Spot kingfishers, anhingas, great green macaws, and the elusive tapir at the water's edge. Photography-focused session with a specialist wildlife guide.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class at the lodge with the head chef — learn to prepare traditional Caribbean Costa Rican dishes using local ingredients. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast after the early morning turtle tour — Caribbean breakfast spread featuring johnnycakes, eggs, fresh fruit, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Floating lunch aboard a private canal boat — gourmet picnic boxes with local specialties, tropical juices, and chilled wine
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the cooking class — traditional rondon stew, coconut rice, plantain chips, and a Caribbean rum punch crafted during the class

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle tours are strictly regulated — no flash photography, red-light flashlights only, and guides must be licensed by SINAC. Tours depart between 20:00 and midnight depending on turtle activity. Wear dark clothing and insect repellent. February turtle activity is not guaranteed but is within the green turtle season.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Tortuguero airstrip to San José (approximately 45 minutes), then onward connection or helicopter transfer back to the Manuel Antonio/Pacific coast area. Alternatively, a full-day transfer with scenic stops through the Caribbean lowlands and Central Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Afternoon at complete leisure — final swim in the Pacific, spa treatment, or hammock time on the private beach. Indulge in a premium 2-hour spa package featuring a volcanic mud wrap, deep tissue massage, and hydrotherapy.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset cocktails on the resort terrace with a private bartender crafting bespoke Costa Rican-inspired cocktails. Special farewell dinner experience at the resort's finest dining venue.

meals.breakfast: Final Tortuguero lodge breakfast — full Caribbean spread before the morning flight
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort upon return — fresh ceviche, tropical salads, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — a curated 5-course tasting menu celebrating Costa Rican ingredients: heart of palm amuse-bouche, corvina crudo, guanábana sorbet intermezzo, prime beef tenderloin with yuca gratin, and a decadent tres leches dessert with a glass of premium Costa Rican coffee liqueur

day_by_day.notes: The charter flight from Tortuguero must be booked well in advance — coordinate through the resort concierge before departure. Confirm resort check-in status and room readiness upon return. Begin packing non-essentials this evening. Request a late checkout for the following day if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the private beach. Last wildlife spotting session in the resort's garden — scarlet macaws, white-faced monkeys, and iguanas are frequent visitors. Optional: final sunrise yoga session on the beach deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout (negotiate with concierge for 14:00–15:00 departure). Private luxury transfer to San José's Juan Santamaría International Airport with a personal concierge escort. Arrive at the airport with ample time for international departure formalities.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with memories of an extraordinary 13-day premium eco-adventure. Access the premium airline lounge at SJO for final refreshments before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the resort — order anything from the full menu as a celebratory send-off: eggs your way, smoked salmon, avocado, pastries, and the finest Costa Rican single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or a curated snack box prepared by the resort chef for the transfer journey to the airport
meals.dinner: Onboard dining or airport lounge — request a premium meal option for your return flight

day_by_day.notes: Costa Rica requires all departing passengers to check in at least 3 hours before international flights. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — do not purchase items made from protected species. Declare any agricultural products at customs. Keep all receipts for duty-free purchases. The resort can arrange duty-free shopping delivery to the airport.
